--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: factorial.pyl - Iterative algorithm benchmark
Demonstrates: while loops, arithmetic, function calls, os.time() benchmarking.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let os = import("os")

fn factorial(n) {
    let result = 1
    let i = 2
    while i <= n { result *= i; i += 1 }
    return result
}

fn main() {
    let start = os.time()
    let i = 0
    while i < 100000 { factorial(15); i += 1 }
    printf("Time taken: {} seconds", os.time() - start)
}

main()

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: fib.pyl - Recursive benchmark (Fibonacci)
Demonstrates: recursion, conditional logic, os.time() benchmarking.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let os = import("os")

fn fib(n) {
    if n <= 1 { return n }
    return fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2)
}

fn main() {
    let start = os.time()
    let r = fib(35)
    printf("Fibonacci(35) = {}, time: {:.6f}s", r, os.time() - start)
}

main()

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: files.pyl - File I/O (sync and async)
Demonstrates: File.open() modes (r/w/a/wb/rb), read/write/seek/tell, async I/O
with waitfor(), os.remove().
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let os = import("os")

fn test_text_io() {
    let f = File.open("test.txt", "w")
    f.write("line 1\nline 2\n"); f.close()
    let r = File.open("test.txt", "r")
    let line = r.read_line()
    while line != none { print(line); line = r.read_line() }
    r.close()
}

fn test_binary_io() {
    let f = File.open("test.bin", "wb")
    f.write_bytes(Bytes([0x41, 0x42, 255, 0, 128])); f.close()
    let r = File.open("test.bin", "rb")
    r.seek(2, 0)
    let bytes = r.read_bytes()
    for b in bytes { print(b) }
    r.close()
}

fn test_async_io() {
    waitfor(File.open("test_async.txt", "w").write_async("async line\n"))
    let content = waitfor(File.open("test_async.txt", "r").read_all_async())
    print(content)
}

fn main() {
    test_text_io(); test_binary_io(); test_async_io()
    os.remove("test.txt"); os.remove("test.bin"); os.remove("test_async.txt")
}

async.run(main)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: input.pyl - User input
Demonstrates: input() function with optional prompt.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let name = input("What is your name? ")
print("Hello, " + name)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: json_parser.pyl - Recursive descent JSON parser
Demonstrates: struct with _init, recursion, string iteration, array/map
building, fs.exists(), fs.read_file(). Full Pyle capabilities showcase.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let os = import("os")

struct JSONParser(_src, _idx) {
    fn _init() { self._src = ""; self._idx = 0 }
    fn _peek() {
        if self._idx >= self._src.size() { return "" }
        return self._src[self._idx]
    }
    fn _advance() { let c = self._peek(); self._idx += 1; return c }
    fn _skip_whitespace() { while self._peek().is_space() { self._advance() } }

    fn _parse_value() {
        self._skip_whitespace()
        let char = self._peek()
        if char == "" { return none }
        if char == "{" { return self._parse_object() }
        if char == "[" { return self._parse_array() }
        if char == "\"" { return self._parse_string() }
        if char == "t" or char == "f" or char == "n" { return self._parse_keyword() }
        return self._parse_number()
    }

    fn _parse_string() {
        self._advance()
        let chars = []
        while self._peek() != "\"" and self._peek() != "" {
            if self._peek() == "\\" {
                self._advance()
                let esc = self._advance()
                if esc == "n" { chars.append("\n") }
                elif esc == "t" { chars.append("\t") }
                elif esc == "\\" { chars.append("\\") }
                elif esc == "\"" { chars.append("\"") }
                else { chars.append(esc) }
            } else { chars.append(self._advance()) }
        }
        self._advance()
        return "".join(chars)
    }

    fn _parse_number() {
        let start = self._idx
        if self._peek() == "-" { self._advance() }
        while self._peek().is_digit() or self._peek() == "." { self._advance() }
        return self._src.slice(start, self._idx).to_num()
    }

    fn _parse_keyword() {
        let start = self._idx
        while self._peek().is_alpha() { self._advance() }
        let kw = self._src.slice(start, self._idx)
        if kw == "true" { return true }
        if kw == "false" { return false }
        return none
    }

    fn _parse_array() {
        self._advance()
        let arr = []; self._skip_whitespace()
        if self._peek() == "]" { self._advance(); return arr }
        while true {
            self._skip_whitespace()
            arr.append(self._parse_value())
            self._skip_whitespace()
            if self._peek() == "]" { self._advance(); return arr }
            if self._peek() == "," { self._advance() }
        }
    }

    fn _parse_object() {
        self._advance()
        let obj = {}; self._skip_whitespace()
        if self._peek() == "}" { self._advance(); return obj }
        while true {
            self._skip_whitespace()
            let key = self._parse_string()
            self._skip_whitespace()
            if self._peek() == ":" { self._advance() }
            obj[key] = self._parse_value()
            self._skip_whitespace()
            if self._peek() == "}" { self._advance(); return obj }
            if self._peek() == "," { self._advance() }
        }
    }

    fn parse_string(s) { self._src = s; self._idx = 0; return self._parse_value() }
}

let parser = JSONParser()
let parsed = parser.parse_string('{"name":"Arthur","level":42,"stats":{"hp":120}}')
print(parsed["name"]); print(parsed["stats"]["hp"])

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: loop.pyl - Infinite loop with break
Demonstrates: loop {} keyword, break statement.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let i = 0
loop { i += 1; if i >= 3 { break } }
print(i)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: structs.pyl - Struct types with methods and static functions
Demonstrates: struct properties, _init, public/private methods, static methods,
named-argument construction, fixed-shape semantics.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct Pos(x, y) {}

struct Player(name, health, pos, _private_prop) {
    fn _init(n) {
        self.name = n; self.health = 100
        self.pos = Pos(x: 0, y: 0)
    }
    fn damageBy(n) { self.health -= n }
    fn status() { return format("Name: {}\nHealth: {}", self.name, self.health) }
    static fn update_players(arr, p) { arr.append(p) }
}

let p = Player("John")
print(p.status())
p.damageBy(20)
printf("{} has {} hp left.", p.name, p.health)
print(p.distanceFrom(Pos(x: 0, y: 5)))

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Raylib Examples
================================================================================
These examples use the raylib module accessed via import("raylib").
They cover windowing, 2D/3D drawing, input, shaders, and simulation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: basic_window.pyl - Minimal raylib window
Demonstrates: InitWindow, SetTargetFPS, WindowShouldClose, BeginDrawing,
ClearBackground, DrawText, CloseWindow. Centered text display.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let rl = import("raylib")
rl.SetExitKey(rl.KEY_NULL)
rl.InitWindow(800, 450, "basic window")
rl.SetTargetFPS(60)

let text = "hello from pyle!"
let tw = rl.MeasureText(text, 40)
let tx = (800 - tw) / 2
let ty = (450 - 40) / 2

while not rl.WindowShouldClose() {
    rl.BeginDrawing()
    rl.ClearBackground(rl.RAYWHITE)
    rl.DrawText(text, tx, ty, 40, rl.LIGHTGRAY)
    rl.EndDrawing()
}
rl.CloseWindow()

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: 3d_cubes.pyl - 3D rendering with orbital camera
Demonstrates: Camera3D, UpdateCamera with CAMERA_ORBITAL, BeginMode3D,
DrawCube, DrawCubeWires, DrawSphere, DrawPlane, DrawGrid.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let rl = import("raylib")
rl.SetExitKey(rl.KEY_NULL)
rl.InitWindow(800, 600, "3D cubes")
rl.SetTargetFPS(60)

let cam = rl.Camera3D()
cam.position = rl.Vector3(10, 10, 10)
cam.target = rl.Vector3(0, 0, 0)
cam.up = rl.Vector3(0, 1, 0)
cam.fovy = 45
cam.projection = rl.CAMERA_PERSPECTIVE

while not rl.WindowShouldClose() {
    rl.UpdateCamera(cam, rl.CAMERA_ORBITAL)
    rl.BeginDrawing()
    rl.ClearBackground(rl.RAYWHITE)
    rl.BeginMode3D(cam)
    rl.DrawGrid(10, 1)
    rl.DrawCube(rl.Vector3(0, 1, 0), 2, 2, 2, rl.RED)
    rl.DrawCubeWires(rl.Vector3(0, 1, 0), 2, 2, 2, rl.DARKGRAY)
    rl.DrawCube(rl.Vector3(-3, 1, -3), 1, 1, 1, rl.GREEN)
    rl.DrawCube(rl.Vector3(3, 1, 3), 1, 1, 1, rl.BLUE)
    rl.DrawSphere(rl.Vector3(0, 3, 0), 1, rl.ORANGE)
    rl.DrawSphereWires(rl.Vector3(0, 3, 0), 1, 16, 16, rl.DARKGRAY)
    rl.DrawPlane(rl.Vector3(0, -0.5, 0), rl.Vector2(12, 12), rl.BEIGE)
    rl.EndMode3D()
    rl.DrawFPS(10, 10)
    rl.EndDrawing()
}
rl.CloseWindow()

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: life.pyl - Conway's Game of Life
Demonstrates: Struct-based grid simulation, Cell/Life structs, GetRandomSeed,
GetMouseX/Y, IsMouseButtonDown, IsKeyPressed, GetTime, color palette array,
panel UI with DrawText, generation counting, variable-step simulation.
Full game-of-life with painting and controls.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let rl = import("raylib"); let m = import("math")
let W = 1280; let H = 800; let CELL = 6; let PANEL = 220
let GRID_W = W - PANEL; let COLS = m.floor(GRID_W / CELL); let ROWS = m.floor(H / CELL)
let STEP_RATE = 0.08

struct Cell(alive, age) {
    fn _init(a, g) { self.alive = a; self.age = g }
    fn revive() { self.alive = 1; self.age = 1 }
    fn kill() { self.alive = 0; self.age = 0 }
}

struct Life(cols, rows, grid) {
    fn _init(c, r) {
        self.cols = c; self.rows = r; self.grid = []
        let k = 0; while k < c * r { self.grid.append(Cell(0, 0)); k += 1 }
    }
    fn at(x, y) { return self.grid[x + y * self.cols] }
    fn reseed() { for cell in self.grid {
        if rl.GetRandomValue(0, 99) < 30 { cell.revive() } else { cell.kill() }
    }}
    fn clear() { for cell in self.grid { cell.kill() } }
}

let life = Life(COLS, ROWS)
let palette = [rl.GREEN, rl.LIME, rl.YELLOW, rl.GOLD, rl.ORANGE,
               rl.RED, rl.MAGENTA, rl.PURPLE, rl.BLUE, rl.SKYBLUE, rl.RAYWHITE]
let PANEL_COL = rl.Color(18, 18, 26, 255)

rl.InitWindow(W, H, "Pyle Life - Conway's Game of Life")
rl.SetTargetFPS(60)

while not rl.WindowShouldClose() {
    if rl.IsMouseButtonDown(0) {
        let gx = m.floor(rl.GetMouseX() / CELL); let gy = m.floor(rl.GetMouseY() / CELL)
        for dy in -1..2 { for dx in -1..2 {
            let px = gx + dx; let py = gy + dy
            if px >= 0 and px < COLS and py >= 0 and py < ROWS { life.at(px, py).revive() }
        }}
    }
    if rl.IsMouseButtonDown(1) {
        let gx = m.floor(rl.GetMouseX() / CELL); let gy = m.floor(rl.GetMouseY() / CELL)
        for dy in -1..2 { for dx in -1..2 {
            let px = gx + dx; let py = gy + dy
            if px >= 0 and px < COLS and py >= 0 and py < ROWS { life.at(px, py).kill() }
        }}
    }
    if rl.IsKeyPressed(82) { life.reseed() }
    if rl.IsKeyPressed(67) { life.clear() }

    life.step()  # (simplified — full neighbor-count logic in source)

    rl.BeginDrawing()
    rl.ClearBackground(rl.BLACK)
    rl.DrawRectangle(GRID_W, 0, PANEL, H, PANEL_COL)
    rl.DrawText("Pyle Life", GRID_W + 16, 18, 28, rl.RAYWHITE)
    rl.DrawFPS(10, 10)
    rl.EndDrawing()
}
rl.CloseWindow()

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Example: shader_effect.pyl - Custom GLSL shader
Demonstrates: LoadShader, GetShaderLocation, BeginShaderMode, EndShaderMode,
GenImageChecked, LoadTextureFromImage, shader uniform time updates.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

let rl = import("raylib")
rl.SetExitKey(rl.KEY_NULL)
rl.InitWindow(800, 600, "shader effect")
rl.SetTargetFPS(60)

let img = rl.GenImageChecked(256, 256, 16, 16, rl.DARKBLUE, rl.SKYBLUE)
let tex = rl.LoadTextureFromImage(img)
rl.UnloadImage(img)

let shader = rl.LoadShader(none, "examples/raylib/test.fs")
let loc_time = rl.GetShaderLocation(shader, "u_time")

let time = 0
while not rl.WindowShouldClose() {
    time += rl.GetFrameTime()
    rl.BeginDrawing()
    rl.ClearBackground(rl.RAYWHITE)
    rl.BeginShaderMode(shader)
    rl.DrawTextureEx(tex, rl.Vector2(272, 172), 0, 1, rl.WHITE)
    rl.EndShaderMode()
    rl.EndDrawing()
}
rl.UnloadTexture(tex)
rl.UnloadShader(shader)
rl.CloseWindow()
```
